dialect.detail: JMA ORCA medical receipt software (JMA standard receipt software), running on Linux with GnuCOBOL. Program ORCS02 is a patient cost-sharing calculation subprogram for inpatient use.
evidence: COPY count 40, CALL count 100 typical of ORCA suite
fixed format, no COMP-3 consistent with GnuCOBOL/OpenCOBOL ORCA codebase

purpose.domain_detail: Japanese medical insurance billing system (ORCA - JMA standard receipt software). Calculates patient co-payment amounts for inpatient claims under Japanese national health insurance rules, including regional public expense subsidies, elderly patient rules, low-income thresholds, and meal/living expense charges.
purpose.summary: ORCS02 is a large subprogram in the JMA ORCA medical receipt system that calculates patient cost-sharing (co-payment) amounts for inpatient hospital stays. It handles complex Japanese health insurance rules including national insurance, elderly patient tiers, regional public subsidies, income-based limits, and meal/living expense charges. The program has an extensive revision history spanning 2002-2009 covering numerous prefectural and national insurance rule changes.

notable_features: Extensive Japanese-language comments (EUC-JP encoded, decoded as latin-1)
100 CALL statements indicating heavy use of external subprograms
764 PERFORM statements indicating complex procedural logic
No EXEC SQL or EXEC CICS (batch subprogram)
No COMP-3 usage (unusual for financial calculations - may use DISPLAY numeric)
Long revision history: 150+ documented changes from 2002-2009
Covers Japanese national health insurance co-payment calculation rules for multiple prefectures
verdict.notes: File is encoded in EUC-JP Japanese but decoded as latin-1, causing mojibake in Japanese text portions. The program is clearly part of the well-known open-source JMA ORCA medical receipt system for Linux. Source truncated at 16000 chars but mechanical indicators confirm full file is ~30,000 lines. No COMP-3 despite financial calculations is notable and consistent with ORCA/GnuCOBOL coding style.
